repo_notes.content: Loadout (crate and package name agent-loadout, CLI binary `loadout`, desktop binary `agent-loadout-app`) keeps one versioned, offline store of MCP servers, skills and secret references and writes them into the native config files of 38 AI coding clients (omp is the recommended client; also Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Claude Desktop, VS Code with GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI and more). The store is a local git repository; every change is one commit. It is a Rust workspace (crates/agent-loadout-core, crates/agent-loadout, crates/agent-loadout-testkit), a Tauri 2 desktop app in src-tauri/ (its own Cargo workspace), and a React 18 + TypeScript frontend in src/.

Sources of truth. SPEC.md is the design contract (sections are cited in code comments as `SPEC 8.3` and so on). docs/milestones/M*.md are completion notes written when each milestone landed: they are history, not a description of current behavior; prefer the code and SPEC.md. Where SPEC.md and the code disagree, the code is current. docs/user-guide.md, docs/concepts.md, docs/cli.md and docs/architecture.md describe current behavior. Generated files, never edited by hand: src/ipc/bindings.ts (tauri-specta, `npm run bindings`), the table between `<!-- adapters:begin -->` and `<!-- adapters:end -->` in docs/adapters.md (test crates/agent-loadout-core/tests/docs_adapters.rs with LOADOUT_UPDATE_DOCS=1), docs/schema/*.json (JSON Schemas from the Rust model types via schemars), and docs/cli.md (scripts/gen-cli-docs.mjs). docs/internal/ holds historical pre-build notes (LANDSCAPE.md, the survey of comparable tools), not documentation of current behavior.

Crate boundaries. crates/agent-loadout-core owns all logic: model, store, formats, adapters, layering, apply, secrets, skills, remote, migrate, paths. It never reads process-global state (std::env, home lookups, the clock): callers inject an `Env` and an `Fs` (crates/agent-loadout-core/src/env.rs, fs.rs). crates/agent-loadout (the CLI, clap, crates/agent-loadout/src/main.rs and src/cmd/) and src-tauri/src/commands/ (Tauri commands) are thin wrappers that build an Env from the process and call core. The frontend talks to the backend only through the typed `Transport` in src/ipc/transport.ts. Errors are typed `CoreError` values with stable snake_case `ErrorCode`s (crates/agent-loadout-core/src/error.rs); display strings live only in src/i18n/en.ts (English only).

Security invariants. No secret value is ever stored in the store or sent across IPC: servers reference secrets as `${secret:ALIAS}`, aliases map to env:, keyring://, op:// or op-env:// references, and a leak scanner (crates/agent-loadout-core/src/secrets/scanner.rs) runs on every store commit. Foreign client entries (ones Loadout did not write) are never modified or removed unless the user adopts or imports them. Ownership is defined only by the machine-local ledger (state/ledger.json, HMAC-keyed hashes, crates/agent-loadout-core/src/apply/ledger.rs). Project manifests (

/.loadout/project.toml and project.local.toml) are applied only after the user trusted their exact content hash (state/trust.json, layering/trust.rs); otherwise targets plan as blocked trust_required and commands exit 7. Client files are backed up to backups/files before every write and written atomically (temp file plus rename or ReplaceFileW) with a post-write self check. One cross-process lock (state/loadout.lock) serializes mutation.

Test conventions. Tests are hermetic: agent_loadout_testkit::TempHome builds a temp root with home, appdata, localappdata and xdg folders and yields an Env plus a RootedFs that panics on any path outside the root. CLI tests clear the environment and pass --home. The 1Password CLI is replaced by the op-stub binary (crates/agent-loadout-testkit/src/bin, op_stub.rs), gh by gh-stub, the OS keyring by MemKeyring, and system git runs with an isolated config (git_env.rs). Client fixtures live in fixtures/. Frontend tests use Vitest with the explicit mock transport (src/test/mockTransport.ts); there is no silent fixture fallback. E2E smoke tests (tests/e2e) drive the built app with tauri-driver. No test may touch real client configs, real secrets, the real keyring or the network.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: What Loadout is and does: the store, clients, apply, secrets by reference, projects, skills, remotes. Summarize README.md, docs/concepts.md and SPEC.md sections 1 to 3. Name the three Rust crates (crates/), the desktop app (src-tauri/) and the frontend (src/), and point readers at docs/README.md.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.purpose: How the crates and processes fit together: core owns logic, the CLI and Tauri commands are thin wrappers, the injected Env and Fs, typed errors, the global lock. Sources: docs/architecture.md, SPEC.md section 4, crates/agent-loadout-core/src/lib.rs, env.rs, fs.rs, error.rs, paths.rs, brand.rs.

pages.title: Core library module map
pages.purpose: One section per module of crates/agent-loadout-core/src: model/, store/, formats/, adapters/, layering/, apply/, secrets/, skills/, remote/, migrate/, paths.rs, local_settings.rs. What each owns and its main types.

pages.title: CLI crate
pages.purpose: crates/agent-loadout: main.rs (clap tree, global --home/--json/--yes, exit codes), src/cmd/*.rs (one file per command), src/exec (the `loadout exec` launcher that never writes stdout), keyring.rs. Reference docs/cli.md and docs/user-guide.md.

pages.title: Desktop app backend
pages.purpose: src-tauri: src/main.rs (tauri-specta builder, collected commands and events), src/commands/*.rs (thin command wrappers, path validation, IpcError), commands/watch.rs (the drift file watcher and TargetsChanged event), updates.rs, tauri.conf.json (CSP, capabilities). How src/ipc/bindings.ts is generated (`npm run bindings`).

pages.title: Store and git history
pages.purpose: The versioned store: <LOADOUT_HOME>/store layout, Store::transaction, one commit per change, commit trailers, tags (including auto/ tags), history, diff, restore, the store lock. Sources: crates/agent-loadout-core/src/store/ (transaction.rs, trailers.rs, tags.rs, log.rs, diff.rs, restore.rs, lock.rs, bootstrap.rs), model/, docs/schema/, SPEC.md sections 4.5, 5 and 9.

pages.title: Client adapters and formats
pages.purpose: The adapter model: AdapterSpec table, mappers, capabilities, detection, locations and placeholders, and the format-preserving editors. Sources: crates/agent-loadout-core/src/adapters/ (spec.rs, mapper.rs, caps.rs, detect.rs, location.rs, mod.rs), src/formats/ (jsonc.rs, toml.rs, yaml.rs, json5.rs, text.rs), docs/adapters.md, SPEC.md section 7.

pages.title: Tier A clients: omp, Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop
pages.purpose: The daily Tier A adapters and their files, shapes, native disable and secret delivery: adapters/omp.rs, claude_code.rs, codex.rs, claude_desktop.rs; the generated table in docs/adapters.md.

pages.title: Tier B, C and D clients
pages.purpose: Tier B (adapters/pi.rs, copilot.rs, cursor.rs and vscode_legacy.rs, the legacy VS Code mcp.json, read only): Copilot and VS Code variants and profiles, Cursor project servers that need enabling in Cursor. Tier C (gemini.rs, antigravity.rs, opencode.rs, grok.rs) and Tier D (windsurf.rs, devin.rs, and the user-scope clients ported from SkillDock in ported.rs): read-only and best-effort rules, YAML and JSON5 editors. docs/adapters.md, SPEC.md sections 7.3, 7.5 and 20.2.

pages.title: Apply engine
pages.purpose: Planning, drift, ownership and execution: entry states, the planning table, instant versus review mode, apply commits, rollback, discard pending, the resolver, and planning cost (each client file parsed once per plan, scoped instant applies, the app's cached plan in apply/cache.rs invalidated by recorded reads and the drift watcher). Sources: crates/agent-loadout-core/src/apply/ (plan.rs, render.rs, exec.rs, cache.rs, ledger.rs, journal.rs, backup.rs, rollback.rs, discard.rs, resolve.rs), SPEC.md section 8.

pages.title: Import, adopt and not-managed entries
pages.purpose: Bringing an existing setup in: `loadout import` scans user files and every known project (trusted or not, read only), groups identical definitions, reports conflicts (--pick, --as, --skip), extracts literal secrets to the keyring, 1Password or env (--extract, secrets/extract.rs), names project-only entries in manifests (`from`), and removes the backups that still hold old secret values (--remove-old-backups); `loadout adopt` for entries that match a store server; the not-managed findings, acknowledged entries (state/unmanaged-seen.json) and the app's Import page, Not managed by Loadout sections and one-line sidebar notice; `loadout skills adopt` (skills/adopt.rs, skills/hash_cache.rs) and `loadout project discover` (layering/discover.rs). Sources: apply/import.rs, apply/unmanaged.rs, src-tauri/src/commands/import.rs and discover.rs, src/app/routes/import/, docs/user-guide.md (Importing in the app), SPEC.md sections 8.6, 11.7, 12.5 and 13.3.

pages.title: Read-only contexts
pages.purpose: Client files and folders this account can read but not write (since 0.4.0). The write probe (access.rs, Fs::write_probe) never writes, runs under a two-second budget and is cached per path and content fingerprint; kinds acl, attribute, owner, share; entries that would write a read-only file are blocked with read_only_target, a refused write at execution maps to the same code, and the exit code ignores it. Refresh in the app calls `recheck_targets` (apply::recheck, PlanCache::invalidate) so a permissions-only change shows; so does a window focus after five minutes. CLI `read-only (<kind>)` and JSON `read_only`; IPC readOnly fields and the app's ReadOnlyBadge (src/app/components/ReadOnlyBadge.tsx). Sources: crates/agent-loadout-core/src/access.rs, apply/plan.rs, apply/exec.rs, src/app/apply/driftTriggers.ts, docs/milestones/M37.md (IPC contract), M38.md, M43.md, SPEC.md section 8.2.

pages.title: Ownership ledger, backups and rollback
pages.purpose: state/ledger.json and the HMAC key, origin created versus adopted, foreign entries, backups/files and restore --files, journals for crash reporting, atomic writes and the self check, `loadout rollback`. apply/ledger.rs, backup.rs, journal.rs, exec.rs, rollback.rs; SPEC.md sections 8.1, 8.4, 8.7 and 9.5.

pages.title: Secrets
pages.purpose: Secret references and resolution: the ${secret:ALIAS} grammar, store/secrets.toml catalog, machine overrides, providers (env, OS keyring, 1Password op and op-env), statuses, delivery modes (env, launch via `loadout exec`, command, inline), extraction on import and migration, the leak scanner. Sources: crates/agent-loadout-core/src/secrets/ (grammar.rs, catalog.rs, providers/, status.rs, delivery.rs, render.rs, classify.rs, extract.rs, scanner.rs), crates/agent-loadout/src/exec, SPEC.md section 11.

pages.title: Projects, trust and effective config
pages.purpose: Project manifests (project.toml shared, project.local.toml private), layering and merge rules, overrides and hiding user servers, effective config with provenance, project trust by content hash, project servers edited from the GUI. Sources: crates/agent-loadout-core/src/layering/ (manifest.rs, merge.rs, effective.rs, projects.rs, project_servers.rs, trust.rs, git.rs), SPEC.md sections 5.5, 6 and 17.

pages.title: Skills
pages.purpose: Skill store (store/skills, store/skill-meta with [source] or [bundled]), installs from git, folders and .zip/.skill archives through a review (fetch and scan first, then `install_prepared` behind the trust gate and the scan gate), full 40-character commit pins (short commits refused), updates with change detection and the script marker, frontmatter, links (Windows junctions, symlinks, copies), project links hidden via .git/info/exclude, scanning client skill folders, the agents CLI folder, listings that read only SKILL.md and metadata (summarize_folder, DetectedClients). Sources: crates/agent-loadout-core/src/skills/ (store.rs, install.rs, link.rs, classify.rs, frontmatter.rs, agents_cli.rs), src/app/routes/install, src/app/routes/skills (SkillUpdateDialog), SPEC.md section 12.

pages.title: Source trust
pages.purpose: Trust in a skill or MCP server source as an explicit, recorded decision (store/sources.toml, synced): repo keys and owner/host scopes (github.com/acme/skills, github.com/acme/*, git.example.com/*; no host scope on public aggregators; separate keys for http:// and git://), once versus always, blocks win, lapses on force-push (ancestry check) or a redirect (renamed or transferred; a redirect only adds a question), official marker. Never implicit: --yes never answers; without a terminal `source_trust_required` unless `--trust-source[=once|repo|owner|host]` or `loadout source trust` (recorded as cli-flag or cli-command; #8 tracks keeping agents out). `loadout source ls|trust|block|untrust`, the app's TrustDialog and Settings > Sources. Sources: crates/agent-loadout-core/src/sources/ (mod.rs, key.rs, detect.rs), model/sources.rs, store/merge.rs, crates/agent-loadout/src/cmd/source.rs, src-tauri/src/commands/sources.rs, src/app/components/TrustDialog.tsx, src/app/routes/settings/sources, docs/milestones/M39.md, SPEC.md section 17.

pages.title: Scanning
pages.purpose: Both scanners. The built-in offline scan runs on every skill install and update and every MCP server saved, updated or restored from a source: rules as data (scan/rules.toml, versioned; state/scan-rules.toml can add rules or raise severities, never remove or lower, "custom rules in use"), Markdown prose versus code, byte-typed files, UTF-16 decoding, 4 MiB per file (not-fully-scanned), not-content-scanned, masked excerpts, verdict = worst finding, cache by content hash in cache/scan. The optional Snyk Agent Scan (#27, scan/external/): off by default, Settings > Security and `loadout scanner ls|status|install|remove|enable|disable|token|run`; a pinned v0.7.1 build downloaded from GitHub and verified against SHA-256 values compiled into Loadout (from the GPG-signed sha256sums; fixture and scripts/verify-agent-scan-pins.*), re-hashed before each use; the token only as a secret reference (an alias that must exist, env:, keyring://, op://; op-env:// refused); sends the skill's files (Snyk redacts secrets it detects), name, scanned path, user name, scanner version and, where its platform reports one, the host name to api.snyk.io; skills only; auto-runs for Git, catalog and update reviews, local folders and library skills on request; bounded runs (60 s, process tree killed on timeout, cancel, Ctrl+C); findings mapped into the same model; not scanned / not understood never block or count as clean; external_scan_required while on and unscanned. Both share the scan_blocked gate (exit 8, --allow-dangerous, Install/Update/Save/Restore anyway); trust never skips either. Sources: crates/agent-loadout-core/src/scan/ (mod.rs, rules.rs, engine.rs, cache.rs, rules.toml, external/), crates/agent-loadout/src/cmd/scanner.rs, src-tauri/src/commands/scan.rs and scanner.rs, src/app/components/ScanFindings.tsx and ExternalScan.tsx, src/app/routes/settings/security, docs/milestones/M40.md, M47.md, M49.md, docs/security.md, SPEC.md section 17.

pages.title: MCP servers from Git or a folder
pages.purpose: `loadout server add --from <GIT-URL|PATH>` and Install > MCP > From Git or folder: drafts from server.json (MCP Registry packages and remotes), MCPB/DXT manifest.json, committed client configs, or the repository itself (package.json bin, pyproject scripts, Dockerfile), pinned to the version or commit (unversioned packages marked not pinned); nothing runs while proposing; dependency and build folders skipped; secrets become references and literal values are dropped; save behind source trust and the scan of files and every launch line; [meta.source] provenance; machine-local checkouts in LOADOUT_HOME/servers/<id> (checkout_out_of_date until `loadout server checkout` or Restore copy); folder sources bound to their machine (folder_on_other_machine); `loadout server update [--check]` and Check for update; review stores and the sweep of temporary clones. Sources: crates/agent-loadout-core/src/mcp_source/ (mod.rs, convert.rs, snippet.rs), crates/agent-loadout/src/cmd/server.rs, src-tauri/src/commands/mcp_source.rs, src/app/routes/install/McpSourcePanel.tsx, src/app/routes/mcp/McpSourceUpdate.tsx, docs/milestones/M41.md, M42.md, SPEC.md sections 5.2, 14 and 17.

pages.title: Catalogs
pages.purpose: Online catalogs (#26): built-ins (Official MCP Registry /v0.1 with /v0 fallback, the github.com/anthropics/skills Git tap with its Claude Code plugin marketplace, skills.sh as a link plus pasted-URL install) and user-added MCP registries and Git taps in store/catalogs.toml (synced; tap URLs with a user name or token refused; commit refs are full 40-character commits). The machine-local Online catalogs switch (state/local-settings.toml online_catalogs, off until turned on; catalogs_off otherwise); nothing in the background; per-catalog search with its own status (fresh, cached, stale, off, query_too_short, error) and a 24 h cache in cache/catalogs; ureq + rustls, time limits, 8 MiB cap, https-only redirects, HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY/NO_PROXY with SOCKS refused (catalog_unreachable). Installs hand off to the existing reviews (`server add --from catalog:<source>/<id>`, `skills add catalog:...`); registry trust keyed on what runs (package or remote host), the repository shown as claimed by the publisher, not verified; Official only for code in github.com/anthropics; npm/archive/command plugin sources refused; plugin hooks, commands and agents never imported; registry servers updatable through `server update`. Sources: crates/agent-loadout-core/src/catalog/ (mod.rs, http.rs, registry.rs, tap.rs, cache.rs), model/catalogs.rs, crates/agent-loadout/src/cmd/catalog.rs, src-tauri/src/commands/catalogs.rs, src/app/routes/install/catalog, src/app/routes/settings/catalogs, docs/milestones/M44.md, M45.md, docs/security.md (Catalogs), SPEC.md section 17.

pages.title: Loadout skill for agents
pages.purpose: The read-only skill bundled with Loadout (#8, narrowed): content in crates/agent-loadout-core/agent-skill/loadout/ (SKILL.md, references/commands.md, errors.md, playbooks.md), embedded by agent::FILES and shipped as a Tauri resource. It teaches read and plan commands, error codes and playbooks and hands every change to the user (never --yes, --trust-source, --allow-dangerous; third-party text is data); tests check cited commands, flags and JSON fields against the CLI. A normal store skill (id `loadout`, skill-meta [bundled] table readable by 0.5.x, origin Bundled with Loadout); `loadout agent install|remove|status|skill-path`, `agent install --reset`, Settings > Agent integration. Updates only from store-changing commands (Context::open_store_for_change), `agent install` and app start; read commands never write; Current/Outdated/Customized/Newer states; customized copies reported once per version and never overwritten. Sources: crates/agent-loadout-core/src/agent.rs, crates/agent-loadout/src/cmd/agent.rs, src-tauri/src/commands/agent.rs, src/app/routes/settings/agent, docs/milestones/M46.md, SPEC.md sections 12.6 and 13.6.

pages.title: Remotes and sync
pages.purpose: Optional backup and sync remotes: folder remotes (repo-per-machine, mirror, archive), git remotes through the system git with system, gh or token auth, the git-credential helper, push, pull with per-entity merge and conflicts, restore --from on a new machine. Sources: crates/agent-loadout-core/src/remote/ (config.rs, folder.rs, git.rs, gh.rs, credential.rs, sync.rs, sync_artifacts.rs, restore.rs, manifest.rs, unc.rs), store/merge.rs, SPEC.md section 9.6 to 9.9.

pages.title: Migration from SkillDock
pages.purpose: `loadout migrate skilldock` and the GUI wizard: read-only import of ~/.skilldock servers, skills, tags, settings and backup repository in one commit, plaintext secret choices. Sources: crates/agent-loadout-core/src/migrate/ (skilldock.rs, scan.rs, mod.rs), src/app/routes/migrate/, SPEC.md section 15.

pages.title: Desktop app
pages.purpose: The React frontend: shell and routes (src/app/App.tsx), typed IPC (src/ipc/transport.ts, bindings.ts), TanStack Query keys (storeQueryKeys in src/app/apply/changeNotice.ts), drift triggers (src/app/apply/driftTriggers.ts), the active scope (src/app/scope/ActiveScope.tsx, ScopeSwitcher.tsx), the English catalog (src/i18n/en.ts), SPEC.md section 13.

pages.title: Desktop pages
pages.purpose: Each page and what it does: src/app/routes/skills (source tabs with Adopt, the update review with trust and findings, Scan with Snyk on a library skill, long lists rendered near the viewport via useVirtualSlots), mcp (including project scope ProjectServers.tsx, the Not managed by Loadout section, McpSourceUpdate.tsx with Check for update and Restore copy), projects (effective matrix, trust review, Discover projects), tools (ToolManageDialog, not-managed counts), install (skill review with trust, the built-in scan and the External scan section, MCP Form or paste and From Git or folder, Browse with the online-catalogs question, per-catalog sections, the neutral missing-Git notice and entry details handed to the reviews), import (MCP import, skills adopt, Discover projects, the SkillDock migration, the sidebar notice UnmanagedNotice.tsx), history (200 commits a page, Load more), settings (versioning, secrets, sources, security with Snyk Agent Scan, catalogs, agent integration, updates, the not-managed notice switch), migrate; the apply drawer and resolver (src/app/apply, src/app/resolver).

pages.title: Command line interface
pages.purpose: Using `loadout`: command groups (including `server add --from` with Git, folders and `catalog:` references, `server update`, `server checkout`, `source ls|trust|block|untrust`, `scanner ls|status|install|remove|enable|disable|token|run`, `catalog ls|add|rm|enable|disable|online|search|show|refresh`, `agent install|remove|status|skill-path`), global options, `--external`/`--no-external` on skills add and update, exit codes (0 to 8, with 8 for a scan block; 130 when Ctrl+C stops a Snyk scan; exec 77 and 78), the trust prompt and `--trust-source`, JSON output, commands that commit and apply at once, read commands that never write. Sources: docs/cli.md (generated), docs/user-guide.md, crates/agent-loadout/src/main.rs, src/interrupt.rs and src/cmd/, SPEC.md section 14.

pages.title: Packaging and release
pages.purpose: How releases are built and shipped: tags v*.*.*, .github/workflows/release.yml (version check, Windows NSIS installer signed with Azure Trusted Signing via scripts/sign-windows.ps1, AppImage/deb/rpm, draft release with SHA256SUMS, latest.json updater feed), the optional Tauri updater, packaging/winget (render.ps1), packaging/aur (PKGBUILDs, validate.sh, verify-release.sh), packaging/chocolatey and .github/workflows/chocolatey.yml, scripts/stage-cli.mjs, src-tauri/windows hooks. SPEC.md section 16.

pages.title: Testing strategy
pages.purpose: Hermetic tests and what each layer covers: crates/agent-loadout-testkit (TempHome, RootedFs, op-stub, gh-stub, agent-scan-stub, MemKeyring, git_env), fixtures/ (including fixtures/agent-scan with the signed pin file and recorded Snyk outputs), golden and property tests in crates/*/tests, src-tauri/src/commands/tests*.rs, Vitest with src/test/mockTransport.ts, tests/e2e with tauri-driver, scripts/verify-clients.md and docs/verify for real-client gates, .github/workflows/ci.yml. SPEC.md section 19.

pages.title: Security model
pages.purpose: Threat model and invariants: no secret values in the store, logs or IPC; leak scanner; foreign entries untouched; ledger ownership; project trust; source trust (never implicit, blocks win, lapses, credential-free keys) and the built-in offline scan before anything from a source is saved; the optional Snyk Agent Scan (off by default, what it sends to Snyk, pinned and re-verified binary, token as a reference only, scrubbed and bounded runs, never --dangerously-run-mcp-servers); MCP drafts that run nothing while proposing, pinned commands, machine-local checkouts and folder sources bound to their machine; catalogs off until turned on, no background requests, untrusted catalog text, registry trust keyed on what runs, Official only for Anthropic's code; the read-only agent skill (guidance, not a sandbox); atomic writes and backups; backups never pushed; Tauri CSP and path validation; skill archive limits. Sources: docs/security.md, SECURITY.md, SPEC.md sections 11 and 17.

pages.title: Contributing
pages.purpose: Developer setup per OS, the gates (root and src-tauri cargo fmt, clippy, test; npm test; tsc; npm run bindings), regenerating generated files, commit style, how releases are cut. Sources: CONTRIBUTING.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml, package.json, rust-toolchain.toml, deny.toml.
